skill.name: personal-finance-visualizer
skill.description: Turn user-provided personal finance records into a local interactive report with spending, income, transfers and cash movement in English or Chinese. Use for statement-based finance charts and period comparisons, not bank-account actions or investment advice.
skill.summary: Visualize reconciled personal finances in a local English or Simplified Chinese report with interactive charts and transaction details.

content.user_title: Visualize Personal Spending and Cash Movement
content.value_statement: Personal statements can obscure spending, income, transfers, and coverage gaps. This skill turns reconciled records into local interactive reports with separate accounting views.
actual_capabilities: Render normalized JSON or CSV as a local interactive report in English or Simplified Chinese.
Show spending, income, transfers, and cash movement across day, week, month, and year periods.
Apply confirmed personal shares, full-refund mappings, and transfer settlements while preserving original bank amounts.
Provide category and merchant rings, area or bar timelines, and searchable, filterable transaction details.
Serve reports from memory through a tokenized loopback URL or export private HTML after an explicit request.
Guide statement reconciliation and request confirmation before finalizing uncertain classifications or transaction relationships.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or later and a modern browser with JavaScript enabled.
Has no universal bank-statement parser; raw exports need explicit mapping, and PDFs require authorized extraction tools.
Supports one two-decimal currency per report, without currency conversion; CSV cannot encode refund or settlement mappings.
Does not access bank accounts or provide investment advice; agent-host retention and exported transaction details remain privacy considerations.

use_cases.title: Review Household Spending
use_cases.description: Inspect groceries, housing, and services while separating confirmed personal shares from original bank amounts.

use_cases.title: Review Income And Transfers
use_cases.description: Separate confirmed freelance income from unknown receipts and reimbursements, then inspect their bank-date cash movement.

use_cases.title: Compare Living Costs
use_cases.description: Compare covered months, inspect daily living costs, and review confirmed loan repayments in English or Simplified Chinese.

prompt_templates.title: Explore A Fictional Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the bundled fictional demo in English. Keep it in memory and provide the local report link without exporting files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: preview the interface without sharing financial records.

prompt_templates.title: Chart A Normalized CSV
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my authorized normalized CSV at [path] for [start] through [end] in [currency]. Confirm unresolved items, then open an English report.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: visualize an existing normalized statement export.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Shared Expenses
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my supplied statements for [period]. Ask about uncertain transfers, personal shares, and refunds before final charts. Use account aliases and Simplified Chinese.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a reconciled report from authorized source records.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Adjustments And Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate my normalized JSON and confirmed adjustments. Compare spending with cash movement, explain coverage gaps, then export HTML to [absolute local path] outside repositories.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: verify refund and settlement effects before an explicit private export.

output_examples.input: Fictional January records contain salary of USD 3,000.00, groceries of USD 300.00, and an internal savings move of USD 500.00.
output: External inflow: USD 3,000.00. External outflow: USD 300.00. Net change: USD 2,700.00.
The internal savings move is excluded from external cash movement.

output_examples.input: A fictional January purchase of USD 100.00 has a confirmed full refund in February. Both records are included in coverage.
output: The matched purchase contributes USD 0.00 to January personal spending.
January retains USD 100.00 of bank-date outflow, and February retains USD 100.00 of bank-date inflow.
The original purchase and refund remain available in report details.

output_examples.input: A fictional incoming payment of USD 65.00 has no confirmed purpose.
output: Please confirm whether this payment is income, an internal account movement, a repayment, or another external transfer.
Without confirmation, the receipt remains outside confirmed income. Final affected charts wait unless a provisional report is requested.

best_practices: Confirm coverage, currency, signs, duplicates, and uncertain classifications before treating charts as final.
Use account aliases and authorized records; pass newly normalized data through stdin without intermediate files.
Keep tokenized report links private, request exports explicitly, and use fictional data for saved screenshots.
anti_patterns: Treating every deposit as income or matching refunds and repayments solely by amount, date, or merchant name.
Uploading private reports, saving them in repositories, or including credentials and account numbers in report fields.
Claiming complete coverage or fully offline processing when only partial statements or a cloud agent were used.

faq.question: Which input formats are supported?
faq.answer: The renderer accepts normalized JSON or CSV. Raw bank exports need explicit mapping, and PDFs need an available authorized extraction tool.

faq.question: Does the report send my financial records online?
faq.answer: The renderer makes no external requests. Agent hosts may retain supplied records; a separate, optional version check retrieves public GitHub metadata only.

faq.question: Can it connect to my bank or move money?
faq.answer: No. It reads authorized records and creates reports. It does not collect credentials, connect bank accounts, or perform financial transactions.

faq.question: Can I combine currencies in one report?
faq.answer: No. Each report uses one currency with two decimal places. Prepare separate reports for different currencies; no conversion is provided.

faq.question: How are refunds and repayments handled?
faq.answer: Confirmed full refunds remove matched purchases from spending. Confirmed transfer settlements adjust transfer and cash views. JSON is required for these mappings.

faq.question: Can I save a report or change its language?
faq.answer: Reports support English and Simplified Chinese. Explicit exports create private HTML containing transaction details; default delivery uses a local memory server.
